body.opens: The store stays in git, as the site publishes its field as it stands, but not as one loose file per object, which grows with every holon, nor as one file, which every publish rewrites: as packs that never change, one per commit, each holding only what that commit adds, with an index read by range from any static host; growth linear in what changes, and the first birth itself cut into commits at a realistic fidelity, since the whole is structural and its evolution topologically divisible. Files divide two ways: by ownership and wholeness, a store per whole, branch as store; and by time, a pack per commit. What may need forgetting is kept as a store of its own, apart from git until sure; a store can always be picked up, left, worked on and come back to. The birth from markdown may end here: the holons are the source now, and any birth after only produces diff-packs. Git is the carrier of the store's files, never its model.
restsOn: the file backend writing packs and their indexes
store.md and remotes.md rewritten for packs
glass not based on git, the author's of 2026-11-01
body.title: The store packed, carried by git

body.opens: A store's point is sometimes not to forget but to pack up and leave: a whole that rests upon another, pointing into it, and stands when carried away, as a stream buffer does. And forgetting is allowed: lifetimes exist, and the end of a thing is decided at the point of its creation. Inference runs are large; the analysis upon them goes as deep as it goes and is made separate, and the runs beneath it may end when their lifetime does. Storage is hot and cold as well, parts of reality; a store given a real lifetime, as things are locked or expired in a bucket. A capacity for the future, pointed to, not yet built.
restsOn: a store declaring its lifetime, by contract
storage that honours it: retention and expiry

body.title: Stores that rest on stores, with a lifetime

body.opens: The markdown dropped but for what lets a new session digest the store in a noble manner: an entry into it and a way to read any holon back as text; and soon a new glass for human interface, an evolved experience based upon this store.

body.title: A glass for the human, born from the store

body.opens: Within a store everything is finite, so holons are simply counted, 1, 2, 3, by order and locality of birth, a reference within the store only its number. Nothing needs to be unique until stores meet: a union gives each store a prefix, as a mount gives a directory its place, and a store born of another is named by its parent, which counts its children. Names are then relative to the union that reads them; randomness, a key or a hash is needed only for a name meant to mean the same in every union, and can wait until it is. The prefix says where a holon was born, never where it stands, which stays a route.
restsOn: one writer per store, branch as store
how a union assigns its prefixes
the code brought to the store
body.title: Names counted in locality, unified where stores meet

body.opens: The store is append-only, so where bytes are written never changes, and an object's address is its place: segment, offset, length. A hash on every object names everything twice, beside the holon's own identity, and costs near half the store with the indexes it forces; it is let go. Segments are one per publish, not per commit, so files are as few as publishes. Each commit keeps one sha256, a fixed-length fingerprint of the bytes it added and of its parent's: a hash of hashes, so one stands for the whole history, any part provable by a path that grows by one step each time what lies beneath doubles. And the lexicon a whole that grows by its parts, not one body rewritten at every new word.
restsOn: the pack format rewritten to segments and offsets
the code brought to the store
body.title: Addresses by position, one fingerprint per commit
